question: does the depth ATANOR learned in CARLA apply in City Sample, which it has never seen?
verdict: YES — measurable, significant, and short of the CARLA ceiling
instrument: flow agreement: Spearman rank correlation between predicted DISPARITY and the flow measured independently by sparse LK tracking. Scale-free (monocular depth has no metres), computed at a few hundred tracked corners rather than 76,800 pixels.

instrument_validated_first.verdict: PASSES — separates truth from noise by 0.63; the previous whole-frame photometric instrument could not separate them at all (span 0.0009 across no-warp/constant/random/CARLA)

read_against_the_ceiling: CARLA ground truth scores 0.320 on the same derotated instrument; City Sample reaches 0.252-0.283, i.e. 79-88% of what perfect depth achieves there.
efficiency: 90% of the depth information in a frame lives in 26.5% of the pixels (|grad I|/Z^2). A dense whole-frame average spends ~73% of its computation on pixels that cannot answer the question, and dilutes the ones that can until the answer is unreadable — which is exactly what happened.
caveats: derotation subtracts the best-fit affine flow to remove rotation, which also removes some genuine translational signal: it cost CARLA 0.63 -> 0.32. The derotated numbers are therefore conservative on both sides.
the two City Sample runs disagree more than sampling alone explains (travel2 read 0.187 in one sampling and 0.252 in another), and higher parallax did not give a higher score, which is unexplained.
rank correlation checks ORDERING only. No metric depth claim is made for City Sample; no ground truth exists there.
supersedes the earlier INCONCLUSIVE verdict, which was correct about its own instrument
